title: Radial dam breaks in a two-dimensional droplet bearing environment
authors: F. Bristy, S. Chandramouli, G. A. Bougas, G. C. Katsimiga, P. G. Kevrekidis, S. I. Mistakidis
abstract: The controlled dynamical generation of radial dam break flows (DBFs) is demonstrated in two-dimensional droplet environments. These ultracold mixtures feature competing mean-field and quantum fluctuation effects and are initialized on a disk-shaped uniform density. Depending on the value of the latter, reflecting also the dominance of attractive or repulsive interactions, three dynamical response regimes are identified. At small densities a moving wavetrain of bright ring solitons is observed (dubbed ring DBF), at intermediate densities a ring kink-dispersive shock wave, while at large densities the flows encompass composite ring kink-rarefaction waves moving towards the center. The emergence of these patterns, whose formation would be prohibited in two-dimensional Kerr media due to wave-collapse, is rooted in the competition between attraction and repulsion inherent to droplet environments, modeled by the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The characterization of the ensuing nonlinear waveforms is further corroborated by reduced models based on the cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. The different wave patterns emanating from dam break flows can be experimentally realized using current state-of-the-art ultracold atom experiments.
summary: This paper analyzes the complex nonlinear dynamics of radial dam break flows in 2D ultracold atomic droplets. By modeling the system with the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation, the authors identify three distinct wave regimes—depending on initial density—that manifest as ring solitons, shock waves, or rarefaction waves. The findings are significant because these patterns are stabilized by the competition between attraction and repulsion inherent to the droplet environment.
main_problem: The study investigates the controlled dynamical generation and characterization of radial dam break flows (DBFs) in two-dimensional droplet-bearing environments.
main_result: Three distinct dynamical response regimes—ring DBF, composite ring DSW, and ring kink-rarefaction waves—are identified based on the initial density, demonstrating patterns prohibited in standard 2D Kerr media.
method: The analysis uses the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE) and its reduced forms, comparing results from 2D simulations, 1D cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger (CQ NLS) models, and simple wave solutions.
model_or_system: The system models ultracold mixtures (e.g., $^{39}	ext{K}$) governed by the eGPE, which incorporates competing mean-field and quantum fluctuation effects via the Lee-Huang-Yang term. The dynamics are initialized on a disk-shaped uniform density.
key_observables: Density ($ho$), phase ($\phi$), and the formation of specific nonlinear wave patterns (ring DBF, kink-rarefaction waves).
important_parameters: Initial density ($ho_0$), which dictates the dynamical regime; the dispersion parameter ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are well-described by the 2D eGPE, and approximations are made by reducing the system to 1D or using the simple wave limit, which neglects certain curvature effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three distinct nonlinear wave patterns: initial disk condition, ring DBF wavetrains, composite ring DSW attached to a ring kink, and radial rarefaction waves with ring kink structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the governing eGPE, identifying the three density-dependent regimes, and then using reduced models (like the CQ NLS) and simple wave analysis to characterize the transitions between these complex nonlinear wave patterns.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses nonlinear wave dynamics in quantum many-body systems, providing concrete predictions for observable wave structures in ultracold atomic experiments that go beyond standard mean-field descriptions.

Illustration of the distinct dynamically generated nonlinear wave patterns emanating from (a) a disk-shaped initial condition of uniform density, ρ0, in a binary 39K mixture within the interaction regime favoring droplet formation. Depending on the value of ρ0 three dynamical structures emerge. Namely, (b) dam break flows (DBFs) composed of ring DBF wavetrains, (c) composite ring DSWs attached to a ring kink, and (d) radial rarefaction waves along with ring kink structures. The insets in panels (b), (c) represent magnified density cross-sections of the ensuing waveforms in the spatial regions marked by the dashed lines.
